title: Rav Chiyya son of Rabbah bar Nachmani
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman regards him as undoubtedly the son of the well-known Rabbah bar Nachmani—arguing that there were not two sages of that name—but finds no instance of him speaking with his father or receiving teachings from him. He was Rav Chisda’s student and always reported in his name, as in the following passages: Sanhedrin 69b and Avodah Zarah 49b have Rav Chiyya son of Rabbah bar Nachmani reporting Rav Chisda. Avodah Zarah 60b instead has Abba bar Nachmani; it should read Rabbah, as in Dikdukei Soferim, and Rabbah is also Abba. Berakhot 43a likewise has Abba bar Nachmani and requires the same correction.

Rosh Hashanah 31a has Rav Chiyya son of Rabbi Chiyya bar Nachmani reporting Rav Chisda; it should read Rav Chiyya son of Rabbah bar Nachmani, as in Dikdukei Soferim. Rosh Hashanah 34b has Rav Chiyya son of Rabbah bar Nachmani hearing Rabbah bar bar Chana’s teaching in Rabbi Yohanan’s name and bringing it before Rav Dimi bar Chinana, etc.

notes.text: The heading’s title Rav is followed, while the checked Rosh Hashanah prints Rabbi Chiyya. The father-identification and proposed name corrections remain Hyman’s argument; Rabbah bar bar Chana is the transmitter, not a single-bar patronymic.

The consulted Rosh Hashanah 34b directly supplies the nested transmission through Rabbah bar bar Chana, Rabbi Yohanan, Rabbi Chiyya and Rav Dimi bar Chinana. Hyman’s exact Dikdukei Soferim readings and father-identification remain attributed edition and genealogical claims.
